purpose: Source-disjoint, bilingual Italian-claim English-evidence evaluation; never tune prompts on these examples before scoring.
source_selection: Official The FA and UEFA public coaching/technical analysis pages, distinct from the previously evaluated Italian tactical excerpts.
limitations: New external sources and source-disjoint relative to prior cases, but human-authored labels are provisional until independently reviewed.
Claims are in Italian, evidence in English: cross-lingual generalization challenge.
Evidence excerpts are curated and supplied directly; retrieval is not tested.
Some contradiction labels depend on interpreting direct tactical opposites, not statistical inference.

cases.claim: Il pressing del centravanti richiede sostegno da parte dei compagni.
cases.source: The FA - How to coach transition
cases.evidence: Crucially, whatever the first response is to the transition, an individual must be backed up by those around them. For example, if a centre forward goes to press a defender, then they need support from behind. Likewise, an attacker who decides to counter needs supporting runs from others.

cases.claim: Quando la pressione sulla palla diminuisce, la difesa deve posizionarsi più in profondità per proteggere lo spazio alle spalle.
cases.source: The FA - UEFA B coaching day three
cases.evidence: So, the less pressure on the ball, the deeper the covering angle and the deeper the defence will need to be to avoid opening up space in behind. As pressure is applied to the ball, then the defence can move up.

cases.claim: Il West Ham ha spinto il Friburgo sulle fasce mantenendo compattezza nelle zone centrali.
cases.source: UEFA - Europa League analysis: Spotting the trends
cases.evidence: West Ham were very organised and structured when defending around the lower third of the pitch. By remaining compact in central areas, they forced Freiburg wide. When the ball did go wide, there was a positive mentality from the West Ham midfield players to cover space and support their full-backs.
